text:
anya: heads-up — customer redwood-cust-445 opened an urgent escalation: p99 spikes and intermittent 504s for Dedicated Standard since ~03:10 UTC. They say attach/scale-up failures. attaching their repro/trace below. can someone triage?

sam: on it. can you paste a specific request id or sample timestamps? also which pool?

anya: pool=dedicated-std-us-west, sample request_id=req_0a9f3c, timestamps in their ticket: 2026-03-15T03:12:34Z -> 03:17:02Z. They included the error from their side:

```
2026-03-15T03:13:01Z ERROR attach failed req=req_0a9f3c code=POOL_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED msg="no warm GPU available, scale-up queued"
2026-03-15T03:13:04Z ERROR attach failed req=req_0a9f3c code=SCALEUP_BACKOFF msg="autoscaler backoff active, queued for 23s"
2026-03-15T03:13:28Z ERROR request timeout req=req_0a9f3c code=504 msg="attach timeout after 15s"
```

anya: customer says p95 normally ~220ms, p99 jumping to ~3-12s and some 504s. They linked the console dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/ops/dedicated-pools?org=redwood-cust-445

oncall-bot: [autoscaler] event: pool=dedicated-std-us-west status=backoff reason="high-attach-rate" timestamp=2065432145
oncall-bot: [provisioner] event: pool=dedicated-std-us-west queued_for_provision=4 timestamp=2065432160

lee: I can see the same in metrics — spikes in attach_rate at 03:11-03:15 and autoscaler_enter_backoff_count jumped. quick grafana query (ops):
```
sum(rate(pool_attach_requests{pool="dedicated-std-us-west"}[1m])) by (reason)
```
link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/-/panel?orgId=1&view=dedicated-std-us-west

kevin: fyi I rolled out a change to autoscaler backoff multiplier ~02:50 UTC (migrated to 2.5 from 1.2) to reduce flapping during a different incident. the change increases cool-down between scale attempts — likely cause of longer queued attach times when we hit short surges.

support-jess: customer is on a critical path (payments pipeline). they reported SLA misses. they're asking for immediate mitigation and root cause.

sam: proposed mitigations (short-term):
- force-provision +2 GPUs into dedicated-std-us-west to drain the attach queue (manual emergency provisioning).
- reduce autoscaler backoff multiplier to previous value or temporarily disable exponential backoff for this pool.
- increase min_prewarm slots to 3 for this pool.
- add temporary fallback route for this customer to hosted model for non-sensitive calls.

lee: I can run force-provision now. command: ```redwoodctl pool attach --pool dedicated-std-us-west --count 2 --force```
I can also bump min_prewarm via: ```redwoodctl autoscaler update --pool dedicated-std-us-west --min-prewarm 3```

kevin: I'll roll back the backoff multiplier for that pool only: `autoscaler.rules.set(pool=\"dedicated-std-us-west\", backoff.multiplier=1.2)` — will do in config-plane and watch closely.

anya: action owners: lee -> force-provision + prewarm (5m), kevin -> rollback backoff (2m), sam -> coordinate with support and update customer, oncall-bot -> keep posting autoscaler events. I'll join to monitor.

oncall-bot: job queued: pool.attach (dedicated-std-us-west) id=job_88bf queued_by=lee timestamp=2065432180

lee: running force-provision now...
```
$ redwoodctl pool attach --pool dedicated-std-us-west --count 2 --force
INFO: scheduling 2 nodes for attach
INFO: provisioning started node_ids=[n-az1-102,n-az1-103]
```

kevin: rollback applied to autoscaler for pool dedicated-std-us-west, multiplier=1.2. watch for flapping, I'll monitor.

oncall-bot: provisioner event: node n-az1-102 status=attached timestamp=2065432250
oncall-bot: provisioner event: node n-az1-103 status=attached timestamp=2065432260

lee: prewarm bump applied. min_prewarm=3.

support-jess: pushed customer update: "We've provisioned additional capacity and adjusted autoscaler settings; monitoring. Apologies for the interruption." they replied: "thank you — please keep us posted"

anya: quick check on p99 from infra metrics: before actions p99=8.9s, after attach completes p99=270ms and no further 504s in last 5m.

sam: confirmed from logs: attach queue drained, attach_latency p99 back under 400ms.

kevin: root cause notes for postmortem: 1) backoff multiplier change reduced scale-up aggressiveness during short surges 2) pool sizing had low prewarm headroom for this tenant's burst pattern 3) no per-customer emergency provisioning runbook documented (we have generic runbooks but not this flow).

anya: agreed. follow-ups:
- kevin -> revert cluster-wide backoff change if not needed, and add automated tests around short-burst attach behavior (P1, 2d).
- lee -> create runbook snippet for manual force-provision & prewarm adjustments with commands and safety checks (P0, 1d).
- sam -> update SLA incident with timeline and customer comms (P0, today).
- ops -> evaluate increasing default min_prewarm for Dedicated Standard by 1 slot (P1, next sprint).

support-jess: i've scheduled a customer call at 09:00 local to walk through impact/compensations.

anya: closing loop here — immediate mitigation succeeded, tracking PMRs and postmortem. will open an incident ticket with RCA and action owners. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: adding incident link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-324 (will attach logs and dashboards)

lee: note for postmortem: include grafana panels for attach_rate, attach_queue_length, autoscaler_backoff_count, and provisioner_queue_depth.

kevin: also add the autoscaler config change diff to the postmortem so we can revert faster in future.

anya: marking resolved for on-call; please continue any long-term work in the backlog.

support-jess: customer confirmed they saw no errors after 03:28 UTC and are satisfied for now.

anya: thanks — thread closed once PMR + incident doc are posted.
